overall_summary: Space-themed content, specifically extreme exoplanets and hypothetical 'What If' survival scenarios in space, vastly outperforms psychology and brain-related facts. Videos with a duration of 19-21 seconds that leverage high-contrast, sensory-rich curiosity hooks (e.g., liquid diamonds, burning ice, supersonic rubies) drive the highest views and engagement.

winning_patterns.pattern: Hypothetical 'What If You Fell Into...' Space Scenarios
winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' achieved 1,023 views and 38 likes, while 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' gained 970 views.
winning_patterns.action: Develop a recurring series of first-person hypothetical survival scenarios focusing on extreme cosmic environments.

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme Exoplanet Weather and Sensory Anomalies
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' reached 1,025 views and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' reached 721 views.
winning_patterns.action: Focus on exoplanets with extreme physical properties (e.g., metallic rain, extreme darkness, precious gem storms) using vivid, high-contrast imagery.

weak_patterns.pattern: Introspective Psychology and Cognitive Brain Facts
weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (10 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) consistently underperform.
weak_patterns.action: Discontinue low-engagement cognitive psychology topics and reallocate production resources to external cosmic and biological mysteries.

next_video.concept: What If You Fell Into a Planet of Molten Iron?
next_video.opening_direction: Open with a first-person POV animation of plunging into a dark, glowing red atmosphere with the voiceover: 'If you fell into WASP-76b, you would face a storm of liquid metal.'
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that the planet's extreme tidal locking causes iron to evaporate on the day side and literally rain down as molten iron droplets on the night side.
next_video.reason: Leverages the highly successful 'What If You Fell Into...' format combined with the proven appeal of extreme planetary weather (molten iron rain), matching the optimal 21-second duration of top performers.

experiment: Test a 'What If You Fell Into...' format applied to deep-sea ocean anomalies (e.g., the Mariana Trench or underwater waterfalls) to see if the survival hook translates from space to geography.
